Physical first-boot and USB registry driver acceptance, audit2628

Every case starts not_run. The generator hashes local records and reads one
immutable Builder source object; it never runs the CLI, probes USB, writes media,
loads a module, reads credentials or changes a device. These commands are for an
owner's separately authorized execution on reserved serial @SERIAL@ only. One
Orin Nano/NVMe or AGX Orin/NVMe/eMMC developer-kit result cannot qualify another.

1. Record the real module/carrier revision, recovery ECID, serial-console endpoint,
   USB physical path, board serial and storage model/serial/capacity. Keep separate
   board power, a serial console, the board-specific recovery/backup procedure and
   its exact flashpack hashes available. Confirm the named owner can restore THIS
   board. The authorization record must separately approve each fresh erase below,
   the named test module, second boots and its eventual removal. No production
   board, shared driver or unrelated storage may be used. The install remains
   interactive; do not add --force, --yes-overwrite-internal or broad cleanup.
   Check the CLI's physical target/erase summary against the independent inventory
   before accepting it. Never infer authorization from successful plan generation.

2. Inventory keys are cli_binary, agent_binary, cli_source_commit,
   agent_source_commit, release_descriptor, release_archive, device_catalog,
   driver_raw, signing_public_key, signature_review, builder_source,
   identity_record, recovery_record, authorization_record, network_isolation_record,
   disconnect_seconds; board {device,carrier,storage,serial,ecid,owner,
   storage_serial,usb_path,serial_console,device_name,usb_address_before,
   usb_address_after}. Use full source commits and actual files. The two USB
   endpoints must be observed link-local addresses on port50051 from this same
   physical board, not invented addresses or another board sharing a hostname.
   The generator supports developer-kit Orin Nano/NVMe and AGX Orin/NVMe/eMMC.
   Record a unique provisioned name @NAME@. Serial/ECID bind the target because the
   first-boot unauthenticated listener's hostname/board checks alone are not
   cryptographic hardware identity. Physically isolate other USB boards.

3. Capture the actual public device manifest, immutable OS version and full
   flashpack descriptor/archive. The descriptor schema is the existing Orin seed
   schema {device,storage,version,url,sha256,size_bytes}. The corresponding catalog
   version must publish the same storage-specific flashpack and devkit kernel
   @KERNEL@, and exactly one wendyos-hello extension for it. Record the published
   raw image, digest, size, modules_load and detached signature. The actual module
   source is pinned Builder commit f72a1b354c80523dc2b092e52e38e44fe56c8d5a,
   drivers/wendyos-hello/wendyos_hello.c. The module logs exactly:
     wendyos_hello: driver add-on loaded (sysext pipeline OK)
   Do not substitute an empty module, copied log line, unrelated firmware driver
   or fabricated catalog. The full archive must be the reviewed bootable flashpack;
   generation hashes it but does not inspect/decompress its rootfs.

4. The published signature is ML-DSA65 over the raw image's SHA256 bytes. The
   catalog itself has no signature format asserted here. Preserve the actual
   candidate Agent's build public-key file and build provenance. Its shipped empty
   placeholder is supported: record signature verification as DISABLED and do not
   claim that a published signature was verified merely because installation
   succeeded. Do not modify the candidate or provision a key just for this test.
   If the actual candidate embeds a key, record enforcement as enabled and require
   its normal verification to succeed; never suppress a rejection or substitute an
   unsigned/development build. Independently review the exact published artifact's
   origin and digest in either case. signature_review JSON binds driver_sha256,
   signature_sha256, agent_sha256, public_key_sha256, the actual boolean
   agent_signature_verification_enabled and reviewer. Preserve actual build/key
   evidence and any independently performed signature verification command/result
   in that reviewed record. Generation checks the binding, empty/nonempty public
   key policy and signature length only; it does not perform ML-DSA verification
   or certify the review. The signature-policy result is separate from USB upload
   and driver activation acceptance. No private key, enrollment credential or token
   belongs in the inventory/evidence.

5. Generate with:
     python3 driver-firstboot-rehearsal.py inventory.json NEW_PRIVATE_OUTPUT
   Compare every inventory/generated/source hash before physical execution. Run
   the generated plan command and compare its exact board/storage/version and full
   flashpack URL with the captured catalog. Generation-pinned GCS URLs must match
   the catalog URL without the generation query and all content hashes. The actual
   install resolves the published version again; if its catalog/artifact differs,
   STOP and prepare a new reviewed plan. Do not switch to --nightly/--pr or a local
   --file shortcut. Verify actual candidate CLI hash and candidate Agent hash
   @AGENT@. The generated commands select a new private cli-config directory and the
   file secret store explicitly. Keep those prefixes when running them; preserve
   that directory until evidence collection is complete, then remove only it.
   Do not modify the operator's normal default-device or auth state.

Case A: install --driver across a genuine powered disconnect

6. Reserve an already identified board whose pre-flash USB endpoint was recorded.
   Use the generated install_with_driver command. It explicitly supplies
   --binary, --pre-enroll=false, --no-wifi and --driver wendyos-hello. A second
   operator watches the serial console and USB/network timestamps. Keep the USB
   recovery cable connected for the entire image write and provisioning. Only
   after the flash writer reports complete, and the CLI reports:
     Waiting for wendyos-@NAME@ to boot.
   disconnect the USB DATA cable for @DISCONNECT@ seconds while the board stays
   separately powered. Never disconnect a writer, remove board power, or interrupt
   a flashing process to manufacture a failure. If the driver already installed
   before disconnection, this attempt does not cover the reconnect boundary.

7. Replug the same physical USB path within the existing ten-minute boot-wait
   window, timed from the waiting message, without restarting the CLI. Record the
   actual changed USB interface/address, mDNS hostname and recovery-to-OS device
   transition. Keep the old/new address and kernel observations in the transcript.
   During the disconnected interval, use the serial console to record the new
   boot ID, kernel, absence of /sys/module/wendyos_hello and absence of the exact
   enabled raw path before replug. A module baked into the image or already loaded
   before this upload cannot prove postflash activation.
   Require wendyos-@NAME@, the exact board type and @KERNEL@ before any upload.
   A genuine address change is required for that subcase; if the address remains
   unchanged, leave address-change acceptance not_run rather than editing interfaces
   or inventory to pretend it changed. Root's protocol fixture separately exercises
   wrong hostname/board/old-kernel responses. Do not connect a decoy physical board
   or falsify firmware identity to repeat those refusals here.

8. Observe driver upload/verification/activation and the terminal CLI result.
   After boot matching, each driver has its own ten-minute upload bound. Record
   "Requested drivers installed" only with exit0 AND the independent observations
   below. A successful flash or reconnect alone is insufficient. If upload stalls,
   retain the failure, allow its existing bound, and inspect the same board. Do not
   start concurrent writers or blindly rerun install. Preserve the flash and driver
   outcomes separately. A missing endpoint or busy module does not prove OS failure.

9. Run generated verify, info and list against the exact new USB endpoint. Through
   the same serial console, run these read-only observations; missing tools keep
   acceptance pending rather than installing extra packages:
     date -u
     cat /proc/device-tree/serial-number
     cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
     hostname
     uname -r
     timeout 15 systemctl show wendy-agent.service --property=MainPID,ActiveState,SubState
   Use the observed live MainPID to hash /proc/MAINPID/exe with sha256sum and
   compare @AGENT@. Do not read Agent configuration/identity keys. Correlate the
   unit's PID and executable again if it restarted while observing.
     test -d /sys/module/wendyos_hello
     cat /sys/module/wendyos_hello/initstate
     sha256sum '/data/extensions/enabled/@KERNEL@/wendyos-hello.raw'
     cat /usr/lib/wendyos-driver-state/wendyos-hello/generation
     cat /usr/lib/wendyos-driver-state/wendyos-hello/replaced-modules
     timeout 15 journalctl -b -k --no-pager -n 20 --grep='wendyos_hello:'
     timeout 15 journalctl -b -u wendy-agent.service --no-pager -n 200
     timeout 15 systemd-sysext status --json=short
   Require the exact raw digest @RAW@, initstate live, a fresh activation generation,
   the actual kernel load message AFTER this attempt, and no
   signature/hash/kernel rejection or rollback in the bounded Agent transcript.
   Preserve a signature-disabled warning if the candidate uses the documented
   empty key; it must agree with the recorded policy and must not be hidden.
   The list JSON must report exact kernelVersion and installed wendyos-hello with
   loaded:true, unreadable:false, stale:false and modulesLoad:[wendyos_hello].
   A sysext merge alone, an old receipt or a log from a prior boot is insufficient.

10. Reboot once from the local console with systemctl reboot, after upload and
    activation have finished. Within ten minutes require a new boot ID, the same
    physical board/storage identity, exact kernel and Agent hash, same raw digest,
    healthy CLI RPC and loaded module with THIS boot's kernel log. Re-run the
    read-only commands and list. Record receipt generation; it may be regenerated
    during boot, so require correct provenance rather than identical text.

Case B: separate unenrolled USB registry upload without device egress

11. Obtain the separate fresh-erase authorization, then run
    fresh_registry_baseline, which omits --driver but pins the same image and
    --binary --pre-enroll=false --no-wifi. Never reuse an already installed hello
    module as proof of upload. Require list absence and no sys/module/wendyos_hello
    before this case. Record the serial boot transcript and generated info JSON with the
    organization key explicitly present and null. An absent organization key means
    enrollment is unknown and does not qualify as unenrolled. Never read private
    configuration contents. Keep the board on separately powered USB only,
    with Ethernet unplugged, no Wi-Fi connection, no cellular/secondary uplink and
    no host Internet sharing, NAT, bridge or forwarding to it. Host Internet access
    remains available for the CLI to fetch the catalog and raw image.

12. Verify generated info has only the intended USB link-local/loopback addresses
    and wifi_status reports disconnected. Over serial, capture:
      timeout 15 ip -json address
      timeout 15 ip -json route
      timeout 15 ip -6 -json route
    Require no device default route or routable address. Independently review the
    host network-isolation record; a disconnected Wi-Fi icon alone is insufficient.
    Do not create/change firewall or routing state with this plan. On this isolated
    board, run generated available and match the recorded name, version, kernel and module list. This JSON
    does not expose signatures or digests: compare those separately against the
    captured published manifest and final raw image. Then run registry_install by NAME. It must emit:
      Device reports no WiFi or routable network address; downloading driver to upload...
    Correlate host-side artifact download with the Agent's incoming streamed upload,
    its verification/apply events and exact installed raw digest. No board egress
    must exist throughout. The message alone is not proof; a direct URL download
    or --file install does not cover this registry fallback. Observe at most ten
    minutes for the CLI download and another ten minutes for streamed installation;
    on expiry retain evidence and inspect rather than launch a second install.
    Require exit0 and all observations from step9. Perform step10 again for this
    independently uploaded driver.

Case C: explicit incomplete-firstboot result

13. This is a separately authorized fresh install_with_driver attempt. Only after
    confirmed completed write/provisioning, keep USB data disconnected beyond the
    ten-minute wait, with board power and serial console intact. Capture nonzero
    CLI exit and the actual diagnostic "OS written, but drivers were not installed".
    Serial must still show the expected OS booted; no driver success message,
    receipt or module may be credited. A flashing error is a different failure.
    Replug only after this CLI has exited; inventory the actual board and record
    the driver as not installed. Do not relabel this case as a failed OS write or
    silently run a retry. A later explicit registry install is a new attempt with
    its own approval/evidence and cannot retroactively turn this result into success.

14. Cleanup only the reserved test module using generated remove_owned_driver in
    an interactive terminal, after identity/list/source checks and owner approval.
    No --force or reset-all. Require list absence, no module directory, no owned
    raw file, and the actual unload log. If removal is refused or another workload
    holds it, leave evidence and follow the named recovery procedure; do not kill
    unrelated workloads or delete sysext state by hand. Preserve transcripts and
    private evidence before deleting the owned host output/config directory.
    Keep every unsupported board, missing address transition, signature review,
    activation/receipt observation, timeout result or second boot as not_run or
    failed. Never derive physical acceptance from generator tests.
